notes: The old Derke import tool is gone (it pointed at Batou's character and could rebuild him as Derke). The four player characters have no level until their player picks a class.

Classes, levels 1-5: Solo (24 + CON HP, +6 a level; Combat Awareness, Patch Up, Called Shot, Suppressive Fire, Extra Attack), Netrunner (16 + CON, +4; Jack In, Breach Protocol, Overclock, Daisy Chain, Daemon) and Techie (20 + CON, +5; Grenadier, Jury Rig, Overcharge, FPV Drone, Ordnance Expert). Level 4 is an Ability Score Improvement.

Players pick their own class the first time they load in without one; everyone starts at level 1. The GM levels the crew from Crew Level in the Actors tab (+1 / -1 per character, Level up everyone, Reset to let a player pick again).

Class features work with FEHA systems: Netrunner RAM and quickhack DC bonuses show in the Cyberdeck, Techie grenade range / DC and the second grenade a turn apply when throwing, Solos ignore weapon load, and the Techie FPV Drone puts a scout drone token on the map that its player sees through.
Healing rolls no longer show the Target cover choice.

Derke is now Batou: an edgerunner on Kurohane probation. New feats Ride or Die, Look Out for Number One and Kurohane Probation, Kiroshi Optics installed, Unity pistol, and seven personal gigs about his probation, the job that got him caught and the people he looks out for. Derke's old sheet is kept in the FEHA Character Backup compendium.

Every NPC has a hand-drawn manhwa/anime portrait and token, framed head-and-shoulders. About 100 new faces replaced AI-looking, black-and-white, chibi and missing art; troops still share one face per unit.

NPC field kit: every NPC type carries grenades and corp consumables that fit its faction, tier and role (EMP for netrunners, recon for marksmen, incendiaries for Rustwater and Scorpions, smoke for officers; Bastion/Helix healers, Corvus RAM boosters, ForgeLine load boosters). New imports get it too.
Grenades cost half: Mk.I frag 150, Mk.III 500, Mk.V 1250 (sticky / homing cost more as before); Ozob's Nose 875.
Every weapon shop keeps grenades in stock: street 3, arms 5, black market 4, corporate 2 at least. Shops restocked once with the new rules.
About half of all gigs also reward two grenades at the gig's level.

Cover is an attack penalty: the attack roll window has a Target cover choice (Half -3 to hit, Three-quarters -6). Token cover conditions add no AC. The damage roll window defaults to the same cover for the damage cut.
Weapon chat cards are short: name, Attack / Damage buttons and tags, without the whole weapon description.
Attack and damage roll windows open on top of the sheet that opened them.
Damage at about 90% of the original (was 60%) for guns, melee, unique weapons, grenades, quickhacks and cyberware: pistols ~19, rifles ~40, snipers ~75 per hit.

Cover is chosen when rolling damage: the damage roll window has a Target cover choice (None / Half -25% / Three-Quarters -50%), shown on the chat card and applied by Apply Damage. Token cover conditions only add AC (+3 / +6) now.
Guns no longer offer a One-Handed / Offhand choice when attacking.
Cover: Half Cover +3 AC and 25% less damage, Three-Quarters +6 AC and 50% less, against guns and melee. Grenades, launchers and quickhacks ignore the damage cut.
Armor soak: worn armor takes 1-7 off every bludgeoning, piercing or slashing hit (light 1-3, medium 2-5, heavy 3-7 by Mk), shown on the armor card.

Weapon load: your heaviest equipped weapon slows you (rifles/shotguns/DMRs -5 ft, snipers and heavy melee -10, LMGs -15). Strong Arms, Power Grip, Reinforced Muscles, Gun Stabilizer, Titanium Infused Bones or ForgeLine Sigma removes it.

Cyberware damage at about 60%, like weapons: Mantis Blades 8d8 -> 4d8+4, Apex 12d8 -> 7d8+1, Gorilla Arms 9d10 -> 5d10+2, Monowire 9d8 -> 5d8+2, Power Grip 5d8 -> 3d8, Projectile Launcher 8d6 -> 4d6+3 (Apex 12d6 -> 7d6+1), Micro Generator discharge 6d6 -> 3d6+2, and the damage bonuses (Berserk, Viral Venom, Kiroshi Hunter, etc.). Healing chrome is unchanged.

Grenades and quickhacks hit for about 60% of before, like guns: frag Mk.III 10d6 -> 6d6, Ozob's Nose 15d6 -> 9d6, damaging hacks 10d6 -> 6d6, 8d6 -> 4d6+3, 10d10 -> 6d10, death burst 5d6 -> 3d6; bleed/burn ticks and flashbangs scaled too.

Damage pass: every gun and melee weapon hits for about 60% of before (pistols ~20, rifles ~27, shotguns ~31, LMGs ~40, snipers ~50 per hit; knives ~14, katanas ~27). Dice type and the order between weapons are kept. Chainsword REDLINE +2d10, Errata +2d8 per earlier hit.
The last reload rules are gone: Helix Self-Charging Cell, Kyokokukamusari Flashbang Magazine, and Metel's reload line.
Gun cards are rewritten whenever their damage changes.

Guns have no ammo or reloading: charges, the Reload action, the shot counter and its buttons, empty-gun blocking, the reload check, Helix auto-recharge and the magazine / reload lines on gun cards and sheets are gone. Guns just attack.
Guns use charges: a gun's magazine is its item charges, every attack spends one (from any sheet or macro), and an empty gun can't attack.

Every gun has a Reload action: bonus action for pistols and SMGs, action for rifles and shotguns, full turn with the DEX check for LMGs and snipers. The FEHA weapon sheet's buttons use the same charges.
Shots already fired carry over. Melee weapons and bows don't use charges; Helix guns still self-charge.

Improvised melee hits less hard and costs less than real weapons: bat 4d6, chef's knife 4d6, butcher's knife 5d6, crowbar / iron pipe / tire iron 3d8, hammer 3d10, batons 3d8 (Murphy 4d8). Military knives, machetes, katanas and guns are unchanged.
Weapon cards show the damage they roll: melee and unique weapon cards that kept old numbers after the balance pass (e.g. Baseball Bat 3d6 -> 7d6) are rewritten, on world items and NPC copies.
A weapon card is now rewritten whenever its damage stops matching its dice.
Melee and unique weapons are no longer re-saved on every load.

Every player hears the Cyberpunk 2077 UI sounds from the table's Forge storage (job board, Market, Cyberdeck, Chrome Manager) instead of the basic fallback set. Volume still follows the Interface slider.
Market DETAILS opens the item sheet on top of the Market (and any item sheet opened over the Chrome Manager or Cyberdeck stays on top).
Foundry warnings and messages show above the Market, Chrome Manager and Cyberdeck instead of hiding behind them.
The Cyberdeck's empty software library says NO QUICKHACKS OWNED // BUY THEM IN THE MARKET when you own none.
Show on city map puts the spot above the GAME PAUSED banner while the game is paused.
Rebuilding gig people keeps their portraits and token art.
New gig people only take their base NPC's look if they're rank-and-file troops, so nobody copies another NPC's face.
Kennel gang members (lieutenant, gate captain, buyer, lookout) use the Kennel Houndmaster stat block instead of the dog's.
A generated gig's person NPC is deleted with its gig files, so generated gigs no longer pile up NPCs in GIG NPCs.

Every gig has its people: 505 NPCs in GIG NPCs / People / <fixer> / <gig>, one set per gig, including the 120 older gigs and anyone a gig scene brings in. Generated gigs make one for whoever their story is about.

Gig people have stat blocks that fit them: fighters use the matching combat NPC; everyone else gets an archetype (child, elder, clergy, medic, official, executive, tech, worker, trader, organiser, journalist, AI, animal, civilian) with abilities, HP by gig level, skills, fitting gear and a bio with their part, scenes, DCs and what they do in a fight. All start neutral.
Built gig journals refresh once to link everyone.

Gigs already on the board follow the gig books: roles instead of invented names and the new maps, with pay, cred, crew and status kept. Built gig journals get the new run sheet with their people linked, ready to drag in.
Gigs are building blocks: invented names are now roles (the bartender, the old priest) for the GM to name; lore names, fixers and the crew stay.
Every gig scene uses a battle map that fits it (a stairwell, a roof, a records office) and the run sheet names each map.

Gig files: a clean copy of each map plus a compact gig journal that docks on the left beside the map (hook, job, scenes with map links, recommended enemies, people, optional twist, endings, reward). Map links take the GM to the map. Nothing is placed on the maps.
GIG NPCs folder in the Actors tab: all 66 enemy types sorted by faction, plus 248 gig people sorted by fixer, ready to drag in. The GM desk shows the count with a Restock button.
Payout panel redone: a They pulled it off panel (pay, loot rows, favour toggle, Pay out at the bottom) and an It went wrong panel.
Four gang NPCs carry their grenades again.
Sound: every FEHA sound (Market, Cyberdeck, Chrome Manager, job board, link-start tones, session intro) follows the Interface slider in User Volume Controls.
Job board: much quieter; opening and closing it is barely audible.

Jobs overhaul: the board is now a contacts list. Fixers come in four levels (Street, District, City, Elite) and open up as the crew's shared Street Cred grows (30 / 90 / 180), or when the GM opens them early.

351 gigs: 231 new hand-written gigs across the eleven fixers plus personal gigs for each character, on top of the original 120. A gig the crew has taken is never offered again; generated gigs only appear once a fixer's written ones run out.
Every gig has its own reward items and fixer favours. The GM picks who gets each item at payout.

GM rundown: each gig shows a step-by-step run sheet (where, checks with DCs, enemies, people, twist, wrap-up). Confirming a gig builds a GIGS folder with map copies (enemies placed hidden), NPCs and a journal with a player handout; one button removes it afterwards.
Twenty new generic NPCs: district gang members and civilians.

Jobs: a fourth hotbar button opens the fixer job board. Eleven fixers across the city post work (120 hand-written jobs, 12 of them personal to the crew, plus endless generated gigs). Players ask for a job and pick their crew; the GM approves, runs it and pays out. Every crew member gets the credits and Street Cred, and Street Cred unlocks higher tiers.

City of Alabastra: the world map is a city map. Twelve districts with their gangs, 103 named places with pins that open the City Guide journal (each with its battle map), and every job sits at a place on it. Active jobs get a marker on the map; the GM can jump from a job to its spot.

Scenes tab (GM only): every map has a wall tag (WALLED, OPEN, PACK, BORDER, GM EDIT, NO WALLS) and the buttons above the list count and filter them. Click a tag to change it. Drawing walls by hand on an unfinished map marks it GM EDIT.
GMs always see the full hotbar; players keep the three-button bar.
Hotbar: just Market, Cyberdeck and Chrome. Empty slots are hidden (a GM sees them while hovering the bar); players also lose the page, lock, clear, mute and menu buttons.

Character sheets: the Spells tab is now the Quickhacks tab (quickhacks with Mk, RAM and loaded state, plus a button to the Cyberdeck); quickhacks no longer show as feats. Species and background slots are hidden. Credits are the only currency shown. The Cyberware Cache has a FEHA icon. Item hover cards are wide enough for their stats.
A gun that shares a name with a quickhack (Optic Zero) is no longer treated as a quickhack.

Prices: chrome within a Mk now follows impact (Sandevistans, Berserks, Second Heart and the Capacity Booster cost double; narrow utility pieces 40% less). Quickhacks cost 750 / 1,800 / 4,500 / 11,250 / 27,000 by Mk. Neural Adaptation Kit 7,500. Subdermal Plating reduces physical damage by 4.
Folders: the firearm catalog folder may be called FIREARMS and its maker folders by full company name; the PC folder is PLAYER CHARACTERS.

Combat test: quickhack and grenade once-per-turn limits, turn-based effect durations and the weapon fired-this-turn mark now follow the fight the character is in. With another encounter selected in the tracker (this world has a leftover active one), the limits were off and effects wore off after a few seconds.

Style pass: character and NPC sheets, roll dialogs, settings and configuration windows, notifications, the pause banner, tooltips and menus now use the FEHA black / red / yellow interface style (core-cp.css).
Content sweep: all 118 weapons fired, emptied and reloaded; all 20 quickhacks and all 18 grenade lines run from a player client.
Cookoff only lists real grenades (it offered guns) and Dead Trigger can break DMRs and LMGs.
Grenade result card no longer squeezes the target's name; the recon scan and EMP no longer treat guns as chrome.
A GM hot reload no longer removes FEHA's message handlers.

Release QA with three GMs and one player. Player quickhacks, player grenades and refund notices now reach the GM: FEHA messages no longer depend on the installed module's socket, which was never relayed.
With several GMs connected, grenade ticks, effect expiry, zone markers and armor bonuses are handled by the active GM only instead of once per GM.
Market: players only see their own characters and no reroll button; a copy of a bought item is no longer refunded as a duplicate purchase.
Weapon sheet redraws when a shot is spent; Cyberdeck quickhack names and the jack-in tray no longer overlap.

Bug test: opening the Chrome Manager for a character who owns cyberware no longer throws an error. The installed manager saved its slot and cost flags as if the chrome were a world item; those saves now go to the character.

Cyberarms are real weapons: Mantis Blades, Mantis Blades Apex, Monowire (Nano Wires), Power Grip Fists and Gorilla Arms appear in the inventory while the chrome is installed and leave when it is removed. Smart links add their bonus with Smart weapons; No Pain No Gain, Knife Sharpener and Blood Depleter add their bonuses to the roll automatically.

Cyberware capstones so every way of playing has Mk.IV-V chrome: Berserk C5, Mantis Blades Apex, Projectile Launcher Apex, Ballistic Coprocessor and the Corvus Apex Cyberdeck are new; Strong Arms, Kiroshi Optics Hunter, Chiton, Throwing Range Servos and the Rockerboy tattoo move to Mk.V; Sudden Aid can treat an ally. Camillo Ram Manager is once per rest.

NPC catalog: 29 ready-made people of Alabastra (street, Yakuza, CivCorp, Marble Vigil, corporate, Navy, civilians) built from the world's own weapons, armour, chrome and quickhacks. The GM imports them from a button in the Actors tab; nothing is created until then.
Looks pass: the chat log, dice results and pop-up dialogs use the same dark HUD style as the rest of the game; cyberware and consumable messages are proper cards.

Sandevistan is now a time stop: on activation you immediately take extra turns while nothing else can move, act or react (C1 a move and one attack; C2-C3 one turn; C4 two; Apogee three). C3 and up attack with advantage.

Cyberware rebuilt to follow Cyberpunk 2077 / Edgerunners: every item has a real effect, passive bonuses apply while installed, and active chrome (Sandevistan, Berserk, Kerenzikov, Blood Pump, Optical Camo...) spends CHARGE, which is the Cyberware Capacity you have left unused. Charge returns on a rest; with too little charge you can push past the limit for psychic damage.

Consumables now do what their card says when used from the character sheet: healing, temporary HP, RAM, or a timed bonus as an Active Effect. Once per Short Rest per product is enforced, a product that would be wasted is refused, and one item is used up. Ghost Key and Network Sweep are reworded as GM-run effects.

Text pass: screen labels no longer use tabletop words (scene, actor, token) or developer names; one name per thing (quickhack, signature, local net, credits). Market and Chrome Manager wording is corrected on screen by FEHA_UI_TEXT.

Network devices (hackable doors, turrets, terminals) are removed. The Cyberdeck has one CYBER CHECK button instead: 1d20 + Intelligence + proficiency, 1 RAM, rolled to chat; the GM sets the DC. Cameras are a GM tool: the Token controls have a Place camera button that drops a camera token owned by the chosen player, who sees through it.

Class-based reloads replace reload points: Pistol / Heavy Pistol / SMG / Shotgun Pistol reload with a Bonus Action; Assault Rifle / DMR / Shotgun / Bow and any single-shot weapon reload with an Action; LMG / Sniper Rifle reload takes a full turn (Action, no movement) plus a reload check (LMG Strength, Sniper Dexterity, DC = the weapon's STR requirement). A failed check means try again next turn. The weapon sheet shows one RELOAD button that rolls the check when needed.

STR requirement now matters: below it you attack with disadvantage (automatic) and can move only 10 ft on turns you use that weapon (table rule), unless installed Strong Arms / Power Grip / Reinforced Muscles / Gun Stabilizer, or any feat or cyberware flagged handling.negateStrRequirement, negates it.

LMG Brace: disadvantage if you moved more than 10 ft this turn (table rule). Sniper Scoped: automatic disadvantage against targets within 30 ft. Ashura and Long Vigil are close-range snipers (no scope penalty, 60/180 ft).
Feats or cyberware can set flags.fleshEnshrouded.handling.skipReloadCheck or reloadAdvantage.

Re-tune under the new reload model (LMG/sniper reload counted at 60% check success): 17 weapons changed, e.g. MA70 12d12, HMG 12d12, assault rifles +2d8, shotguns up, Black Requiem 7d20+28, Borg4a 29d6, Nekomata 4d20+54, Sunlance 1d20+90. Single hits are capped near 100 average; capped single-shot weapons keep their power rating so price reflects the alpha strike.
Disadvantage is applied through dnd5e.preRollAttackV2, so it works from the weapon sheet and the normal item roll.
